verses.text: And as soon as it was morning, after holding a consultation, the chief priests, with the elders and scribes and the entire Sanhedrin bound Jesus, led Him away, and delivered Him over to Pilate.
And Pilate questioned Him, “Are You the King of the Jews?” And in response to him, He said, “You say so.”
And the chief priests commenced accusing Him of many things.
And Pilate again was questioning Him, saying, “Do you not respond to anything? See how many accusations they are bringing against You!”
But Jesus did not respond to anything further, so that Pilate marvelled.
Now at the feast, he habitually released for them one prisoner whom they requested.
And the one called Barabbas had been imprisoned with his* fellow insurgents who had committed murder during the uprising.
And coming up, the crowd began requesting him to do* just as he had habitually done for them.
So Pilate replied to them, saying, “Do you want me to release for you the King of the Jews?”
For he knew that it was because of envy the chief priests* had delivered Him over.
But the chief priests incited the crowd so that he would release Barabbas for them instead.
And Pilate, responding again, kept saying to them, “Then what do you want me to do with the One whom you call the King of the Jews?”
And they cried aloud again, “Crucify Him!”
And Pilate was saying to them, “Why, what evil has He done?” But they cried aloud all the more, “Crucify Him!”
So Pilate, wanting to do what was satisfactory to the crowd, released Barabbas for them. And when he had Jesus flogged, he delivered Him to be crucified.
Now the soldiers led Him away into the palace (that is, the Praetorium*) and called together all the cohort.
And they put a purple cloak on Him, and having twisted together a crown of thorns, they placed it on Him.
And they began to pay homage to Him, “Hail, King of the Jews!”
And they kept striking His head with a reed and spitting on Him; and bending their* knees, they performed obeisance to Him.
And when they had derided Him,* they took off His purple cloak and put His own garments on Him. And they led Him out in order to crucify Him.
And they compelled a certain man, Simon a Cyrenian, the father of Alexander and Rufus, who was passing by and coming from the country, to carry His cross.
And they brought Him to the place Golgotha (which is translated, Place of a Skull).
And they attempted to offer Him wine mixed with myrrh, but He did not take it.
And they crucified Him and divided His garments, casting lots for them, to determine* who should take what.
Now it was the third hour,* and they crucified Him.
And the inscription of the accusation against Him was written, “The King of the Jews.”
And with Him they crucified two robbers, one on His right and one on His left.*
And those passing were speaking evil against Him, shaking their heads and saying, “Aha! The One who would destroy the temple and build it in three days,
save Yourself by descending from the cross!
Similarly, the chief priests, along with the scribes, were deriding Him to one another, saying, “He saved others; He cannot save Himself!
Let the Christ, the King of Israel, descend now from the cross, so that we may see and believe! Even those who were crucified with Him were defaming Him.
Now when the sixth hour* arrived, darkness fell over the whole land until the ninth hour.*
And at the ninth hour, Jesus shouted with a loud voice, “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?” (which is translated, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?” )*
And some of those standing by, having heard it, were saying, “Behold, He is calling Elijah!”
And someone ran and filled a sponge with sour wine, placed it on a reed, and offered Him a drink, saying, “Let Him be! Let us see if Elijah is coming to take Him down.”
But Jesus uttered a loud cry and breathed His last.
And the curtain of the temple was split in two from top to bottom.
And when the centurion, who was standing opposite Him, saw that He breathed His last in this way, he said, “Truly this man was the Son of God!”
Now there were also women watching from a distance, among whom were Mary Magdalene, and Mary, the mother of James the Less and Joses, and Salome,
who had been following Him and ministering to Him* when He was in Galilee, and many other women* who had come up with Him to Jerusalem.
And when evening had already arrived, since it was the day of Preparation, that is, the day before the Sabbath,
Joseph of Arimathea, a respected member of the Council, who was also himself waiting for kingdom of God, exercised courage and went to Pilate and requested the body of Jesus.
Now Pilate wondered that He was already dead, and calling the centurion to him, he questioned if He had already died.
And having learned of it from the centurion, He granted the corpse to Joseph.

And when he had bought a linen cloth and taken Him down, he wrapped Him in the linen cloth and laid Him in a tomb which had been cut from the rock. And he rolled a stone against the entrance of the tomb.

Now Mary Magdalene and Mary, the mother of Joses, were watching where He was laid. 4 Or So Pilate questioned Him again 7 Greek the . verses.text: Now when the Sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene, and Mary, the mother of James, and Salome* bought spices, so that they might come and anoint Him.
And very early on the first day of the week, they came to the tomb after the sun had risen.
And they were saying among themselves, “Who will roll away the stone for us from the entrance of the tomb?”
But when they looked up, they saw that the stone had been rolled away—for it was exceedingly large.
And entering the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, clothed in a white robe, and they were overwhelmed with astonishment.
But he said to them, “Do not be overwhelmed with astonishment. You are seeking Jesus, the Nazarene,* the One who was crucified. He has been raised! He is not here. See the place where they laid Him.
But go, tell His disciples and Peter that He is going before you to Galilee. There you will see Him, just as He said to you.”
And after going out, they fled from the tomb, for trembling and amazement had taken hold of them. And they said nothing to anyone, for they were afraid.*
[[Now when He arose early on the first day of the week, He first appeared to Mary Magdalene, from whom He had cast out seven demons.
She, having gone, reported it to those who were with Him, as they were grieving and weeping.
And they, having heard that He was alive and had been seen by her, disbelieved it.
Now after these things, He appeared in a different form to two of them as they were walking, while they were going into the country.
And they, having gone away, reported it to the rest, but they did not believe them.

And later, as they were reclining at the table, He appeared to the eleven. He then rebuked their unbelief and hardness of heart, for they did not believe those who had seen Him after He had been raised.*
And He said to them, “Going * into all the world, preach the gospel to the whole creation.
The one who has believed and has been baptised will be saved, but the one who has not believed will be condemned.
And these signs will accompany those who have believed: In My name they will cast out demons, they will speak in new tongues;
they will take up serpents with their hands; * and if they drink anything deadly, it will never hurt them; they will lay their hands on the sick, and they will get well.”
So then, after the Lord Jesus had spoken to them, He was taken up into heaven, and He sat down at the right hand of God.

And they, having gone out, preached everywhere, while the Lord was working together with them and confirming the word by the signs that accompanied it.*]]* 1 One ancient Greek manuscript, continuing the narrative from 15:47, omits the expression when the Sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene, and Mary, the mother of James, and Salome, so that it reads from 15:47 as: Now Mary Magdalene and Mary, the mother of Joses, were watching where He was laid, and they bought spices, so that they might come and anoint Him 6 Two ancient Greek manuscripts omit the appositive phrase the Nazarene 8 Some ancient manuscripts include the shorter ending of Mark, which is given as: And they promptly reported all the things they had been commanded to those around Peter. And after these things, Jesus Himself also sent out, through them, the holy and imperishable preaching of eternal salvation, extending from the east to the west.
